independent.summary: The relay still reads as the connector, not the caller: on the Responses-API path the model's search_entities/get_entity run through mcpWorkspaceId(), which resolves Settings.mcpUserId's workspace, so any chat user on that path gets answers out of the MCP user's graph rather than their own — a cross-tenant read in a multi-tenant deployment. The change closes the write half and documents this in the Decision Log as out of scope, but docs/api.md's new POST /chat note says only "tools are read-only on both paths" and never warns that the reads are not the caller's workspace.

grades.reason: It restates the bug this change fixes and its own scenario refutes it — the read-only session registers no write tools, so create_entity is unreachable (verified in routes/mcp.js writeTool() and the probe in chatMcpRelay.test.js), meaning the write does not land.

triageGrades.reason: The change is entirely about authorization scope on /mcp sessions (write-tool registration, scope header, 403 on scope mismatch).
It edits the code that attaches MCP_BEARER_TOKEN to an outbound third-party request and documents that credential's identity semantics in .env.example.
Nothing in the diff touches usage metering, budget checks, or billing — chat's spend path is unchanged.
It changes registration of the ten write tools, including the delete/removal tools, so the destructive-operation surface is directly altered (narrowed).
mcpToolDef() changes what is sent to the provider's Responses API — allowed_tools plus a new header on the tool definition.
No version bump, migration, or deploy/config rollout change; only a commented env-var example alongside code and tests.

summary: The single finding is a restatement of the bug the change fixes, with a self-contradicting scenario, and the triage — while correct on all six keys — is the only part of the review that carries any value.
